3. Defendant No. 3 petitioner appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement denying that he was a guarantor for the letters of credit and stated that he never signed letters of guarantee but the suit was decreed on contest on 27-5-2001 against all the defendants. In fact, only defendant No. 3 petitioner contested the suit and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 did not contest the same. There-after, the decree-holder Bank initiated Artha Jari Case No. 17 of 2003 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka (the Adalat, in short) for realization of the decretal dues. In the execution case, the Bank filed an application on 5-10-2005 for exempting the other judgment-debtors and to proceed with the execution case against the defendant No. 3 petitioner as guarantor of the loan by attachment of his provident fund, gratuity. Whereupon, the learned Judge of the Adalat attached the General Provident Fund and gratuity of the petitioner in the execution case. 

 6. Mr Md Sorforj Meah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner contends that the petitioner was not a guarantor for the loan (letter of credit) although he was shown as guarantor of the loan and that only the defendant-petitioner contested the suit but the suit was decreed on contest against all of them. He next contends that as per section 3 of the Provident Fund Act, 1925 (the Act, in brief) service benefit, such as, GP Fund, gratuity and other benefits cannot be attached by the any Court in any manner and, as such, the impugned attachment of GP Fund and gratuity is illegal and without jurisdiction. He further contends that the order of attachment is in violation of the provision of section 6 (5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain, in short) and therefore, the impugned order is without lawful authority and liable to be struck down. 

 9. It transpires from the materials on record (Annexure-A to the Writ Petition) that the Bank filed Money Suit No. 4 of 1998 for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 12,97,460.97 as stood on 31-5-1998 and in that suit the petitioner AA Manzurul Haque, Principal Officer, Rupali Bank Ltd. Dilkusha Branch, Dhaka was impleaded as defendant No. 3 as guarantor of the loan (L/C). It further transpires from the materials on record that defendant No. 3 contested the suit by filing written statement and denied that he was a guarantor of the loan. It further appears from the judgment and decree (Annexure-C to the Writ Petition) that the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka passed judgment and decree by taking evidence and considering the evidence on record. 

 10. Admittedly, defendant No. 3 contested the suit and it was decreed on contest against him but defendant No. 3 petitioner did not file any appeal challenging the judgment and decree in the appellate forum. Therefore, there is no scope to raise any question about the legality of the judgment and decree in this writ petition. 

 11. However, the question to be decided in this rule is whether the gratuity and provident fund may be attached for realization of decretal dues in execution of a decree.
